configuration: IJN Shokaku, December 1941; full load reference draft 8.87 m

sources.title: The Shokakus — Pearl Harbor to Leyte Gulf
sources.author: Hajime Fukaya; edited by Martin E. Holbrook
sources.basis: Contemporary postwar account: principal dimensions, machinery count and starboard island/funnel arrangement.
sources.limitations: Lists ten triple mounts instead of twelve and conflicts with later descriptions; not used as sole armament authority.

sources.title: Shokaku arrangement, labelled 1941 by host
sources.date: 1941 configuration asserted; drawing creation date unknown
sources.basis: Secondary raster arrangement; common-scale top and both profiles; relative equipment stations.
sources.limitations: Original drawing attribution unresolved. No original hull offset table. Uniform longitudinal registration: stern x38 px, bow x4705 px over 257.5 m on the 4751 px raster. Local vertical draft differs slightly from nominal load.

sources.title: Shokaku launch and early service; Zuikaku gunfire, November 1941
sources.basis: Period photographs of stem, overall silhouette and open Type 89 mounts; sister-ship gun photograph is qualified class evidence.
sources.limitations: Perspective views and limited scan resolution; archive accession still to verify.

sources.title: Shokaku-class dimensions, armor and air group
sources.basis: Cross-check of 242.2 m flight deck, 72 operational aircraft, 46/165 mm belt and 65/132 mm protective decks.
sources.limitations: Secondary summary. Exact armor boundaries, material grades and loaded displacement need primary plan confirmation.

sources.title: Japan 12.7 cm/40 Types 88 and 89
sources.basis: A1 and gas-proof A1 Mod 2 fit; variant dimensions, mounting operation, rate and recoil, cross-checked against primary S09. Complete gun length 5.284 m, bore 5.080 m, trunnion height 2.49 m and recoil 0.45 m.
sources.limitations: Local fork, loading platform, controls and gas-hood dimensions remain estimates. Photographs depict the weapon family; the Balikpapan coastal mounting does not establish the carrier enclosure.
photoProvenance: US Navy NH 73018, c.1932: open Type 89 mount, Haguro in background; mirrored by NavWeaps.
Australian War Memorial 119739: captured Balikpapan coastal twin; mirrored by NavWeaps.

sources.title: Japan 25 mm/60 Type 96
sources.basis: Triple mount, receiver/magazine arrangement, muzzle speed and period photographs.
sources.limitations: Local mechanism offsets and smoke-cover dimensions need further station-specific evidence.
sources.photoProvenance: US Navy photograph of a captured triple mount, Guadalcanal 1942, mirrored by NavWeaps; family evidence, not Shokaku station dimensions.

sources.title: US Navy destroyer gunfire, bomb and kamikaze war damage report
sources.basis: Type 99 No. 25 250 kg bomb, approximately 130 lb explosive; gameplay rounds use 60 kg.
sources.limitations: Shared game contact fuze does not reproduce historical semi-armor-piercing fuze behavior.

sources.title: Japanese World War II torpedoes — Type 91 Mod 2
sources.basis: 450 mm aerial torpedo, 5.486 m (216 inches) for Mod 2, 42 knots and 2000 m range. The shorter 5.275 m dimension belongs to Mod 1.
sources.limitations: Damage, depth, arming and failure rates remain game calibration.

sources.title: Japanese Naval Guns and Mounts, Article 1 — Mounts under 18 inches, O-47(N)-1
sources.author: U.S. Naval Technical Mission to Japan
sources.basis: Primary technical report. Printed pages 41–45 describe and photograph the Type 89 mount. Enclosure G (printed p65, PDF index68) provides side/front/top arrangements; H (p66, index69) shows the rammer. Four upper recoil cylinders, breech and spring rammer, rear moving loader platform, right-side fuze apparatus and bearing/fork layout informed the original recipe.
sources.limitations: Report is postwar weapon-family evidence. Its general arrangement does not establish the exact 1941 carrier gas hood, station stops or every local part dimension. Scanned plate includes a truncated barrel and must not be scaled from its visible barrel length.

sources.title: Shokaku at Yokosuka immediately after completion, 23 August 1941
sources.author: Period photographers unknown; Kure/Yamato Museum collection and NHHC NH 73066
sources.basis: Higher-resolution dated photographs. Corroborate compact stepped island, solid wing bulwarks, upper forward glazing, island room below the flight-deck edge with launch underneath, and open two-level stern boat stowage with deep portal supports.
sources.limitations: Photographic perspective is qualitative, not a replacement for scaled plan coordinates. Ship is immediately after completion, not a load record for 7 December. Hidden hull sections remain estimated. NHHC direct download failed during this review; retained NH 73066 is the Commons mirror with archival identification.

sources.title: Shokaku Aircraft Carrier (1941), two-page three-view plan
sources.author: Hubert Cance
sources.date: Modern illustration of the 1941 configuration; publication date not identified
sources.basis: Creator identifies his two-page three-view drawing for publisher Caraktere. The visible arrangement strongly resembles S02; used to cross-check interpretation of bridge/afterdeck shapes.
sources.limitations: Modern reconstruction, not an authenticated 1941 shipyard drawing. Relationship to the exact S02 raster remains an inference; no unsupported original-plan attribution. Copyright retained by artist, external preview not included in production assets.
